title: Computer Science Fundamentals
subtitle: From binary to algorithms — a complete foundation.

teacher.name: Prof. David Miller
teacher.bio: 20 years teaching CS at MIT. Author of 3 textbooks.

subject: Computer Science

sponsor.name: Google
sponsor.tagline: Building the next generation of engineers.

description: A complete introduction to computer science — from how computers work at the lowest level to writing your first algorithms. No prior experience needed.
what_you_learn: How computers represent and process data
Core algorithmic thinking and problem solving

lectures.title: What is a Computer?
lectures.description: We start from scratch. What is computation? How do machines think?

materials.title: Introduction to Computing (MIT Lecture 1)
materials.description: The foundational lecture. Covers what computation means.

materials.title: Binary and How Computers Store Data
materials.description: How 0s and 1s represent everything from text to images.

materials.title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs — Chapter 1
materials.author: Abelson & Sussman
materials.description: The legendary SICP. Chapter 1 introduces the elements of programming.

materials.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
materials.author: Alan Turing, 1950
materials.description: The paper that started AI. Turing asks: Can machines think?

lectures.title: Algorithms and Problem Solving
lectures.description: How to think algorithmically. Sorting, searching, and complexity.

materials.title: Introduction to Algorithms (MIT 6.006)
materials.description: Core algorithmic thinking from MIT's famous 6.006 course.

materials.title: Big O Notation Explained
materials.description: How we measure algorithm efficiency.

materials.title: Sorting Algorithms Visualized
materials.description: Bubble sort, merge sort, quick sort — visualized.

materials.title: Introduction to Algorithms (CLRS) — Chapter 2
materials.author: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein
materials.description: The algorithms bible. Chapter 2 covers insertion sort and loop invariants.

materials.title: A Note on Two Problems in Connexion with Graphs
materials.author: Dijkstra, 1959
materials.description: The original Dijkstra shortest path paper. Short and readable.

lectures.title: Data Structures
lectures.description: Arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and graphs.

materials.title: Data Structures: Arrays and Linked Lists
materials.description: CS50's introduction to fundamental data structures.

materials.title: Trees and Binary Search Trees
materials.description: How tree structures organize data hierarchically.

materials.title: Hash Tables Explained
materials.description: The most important data structure in software engineering.

materials.title: The Algorithm Design Manual — Chapter 3
materials.author: Steven Skiena
materials.description: Practical guide to choosing the right data structure.

lectures.title: How the Internet Works
lectures.description: Protocols, packets, HTTP, DNS, and how the web is built.

materials.title: How the Internet Works (CS50)
materials.description: David Malan explains the internet from packets to HTTPS.

materials.title: DNS Explained in 100 Seconds
materials.description: How domain names resolve to IP addresses.

materials.title: A Protocol for Packet Network Intercommunication
materials.author: Cerf & Kahn, 1974
materials.description: The paper that defined TCP/IP. The founding document of the internet.

lectures.title: Memory, Operating Systems & Abstraction
lectures.description: How computers manage memory, run programs, and why abstraction matters.

materials.title: Memory Management and the Stack/Heap
materials.description: Stack vs heap, memory allocation, garbage collection.

materials.title: Operating Systems in 45 Minutes
materials.description: What an OS actually does — process scheduling, virtual memory, syscalls.

materials.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces — Chapters 1-4
materials.author: Arpaci-Dusseau
materials.description: Free online OS textbook. Best intro to operating system concepts.

materials.title: The UNIX Time-Sharing System
materials.author: Ritchie & Thompson, 1974
materials.description: The original UNIX paper. Still readable and historically essential.

title: Biology: Life from Molecules to Ecosystems
subtitle: Understanding living systems from cells to the biosphere.

teacher.name: Dr. Amara Osei
teacher.bio: PhD Botany. Researches plant adaptation in sub-Saharan Africa.

subject: Biology

sponsor.name: Bayer
sponsor.tagline: Investing in the scientists of tomorrow.

description: A rigorous introduction to biology — from how molecules form life to how ecosystems maintain balance. Designed for students who've never studied biology formally.

lectures.title: The Cell — Unit of Life
lectures.description: What is a cell? How do prokaryotes and eukaryotes differ?

materials.title: Introduction to the Cell (Khan Academy)
materials.description: Overview of cell structure and function.

materials.title: Prokaryotes vs Eukaryotes
materials.description: The fundamental division in all living things.

materials.title: The Structure of the Cell Membrane
materials.author: Singer & Nicolson, 1972
materials.description: The fluid mosaic model — how membranes actually work.

lectures.title: DNA, RNA, and the Central Dogma
lectures.description: How genetic information is stored, copied, and expressed.

materials.title: DNA Structure and Replication
materials.description: The double helix and how DNA copies itself.

materials.title: Transcription and Translation
materials.description: How DNA becomes RNA becomes protein.

materials.title: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
materials.author: Watson & Crick, 1953
materials.description: The most important paper in biology. One page. Changed everything.

lectures.title: Photosynthesis and Energy
lectures.description: How plants capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy.

materials.title: Photosynthesis (CrashCourse Biology)
materials.description: Fast, visual overview of photosynthesis.

materials.title: Light Reactions and the Calvin Cycle
materials.description: Deep dive into the two stages of photosynthesis.

materials.title: Campbell Biology — Chapter 10: Photosynthesis
materials.author: Urry et al.
materials.description: The standard university biology text. Chapter 10 is the definitive treatment.

lectures.title: Evolution and Natural Selection
lectures.description: Darwin's insight and 160 years of evidence.

materials.title: Evolution (CrashCourse)
materials.description: Natural selection explained with clear examples.

materials.title: Evidence for Evolution
materials.description: Fossil record, comparative anatomy, molecular evidence.

materials.title: On the Origin of Species — Chapter 4
materials.author: Charles Darwin, 1859
materials.description: Chapter 4: Natural Selection. Darwin at his clearest.

lectures.title: Ecosystems and the Biosphere
lectures.description: Energy flow, nutrient cycles, and how ecosystems maintain balance.

materials.title: Ecosystem Ecology (Khan Academy)
materials.description: Food webs, energy pyramids, nutrient cycles.

materials.title: The Carbon Cycle
materials.description: How carbon moves through living and non-living systems.

title: Mathematics for Everyone
subtitle: Algebra, calculus, and statistics from first principles.

teacher.name: Prof. Priya Sharma
teacher.bio: Professor of Applied Mathematics. Known for making calculus intuitive.

subject: Mathematics
description: Math doesn't have to be intimidating. This course builds from algebra through calculus to statistics with visual intuition first and formulas second.
what_you_learn: Derivatives and what they mean geometrically

lectures.title: Algebra and Functions
lectures.description: Variables, equations, functions — the language of mathematics.

materials.title: Essence of Algebra (3Blue1Brown)
materials.description: Visual, intuitive algebra from the best math communicator alive.

materials.title: Functions and Their Graphs
materials.description: What a function is and how to read its graph.

lectures.title: The Derivative — Change and Motion
lectures.description: What calculus actually is. The geometric meaning of the derivative.

materials.title: Essence of Calculus (3Blue1Brown)
materials.description: The single best introduction to calculus ever made.

materials.title: Derivatives — Formal Definition
materials.description: From the geometric intuition to the limit definition.

materials.title: Calculus Made Easy — Chapters 1-5
materials.author: Silvanus Thompson, 1910
materials.description: The most readable calculus book ever written. Free and still the best.

lectures.title: Integration — Area and Accumulation
lectures.description: What integration means geometrically. The fundamental theorem of calculus.

materials.title: Integration and the Fundamental Theorem (3Blue1Brown)
materials.description: The most beautiful result in calculus, made visual.

materials.title: Integration Techniques
materials.description: Substitution, integration by parts, and when to use each.

lectures.title: Probability and Counting
lectures.description: How to reason about uncertainty. Combinatorics and probability.

materials.title: Probability (CrashCourse Statistics)
materials.description: Intuitive introduction to probability theory.

materials.title: Bayes Theorem Explained
materials.description: The most important theorem in statistics, explained with examples.

lectures.title: Statistics and Data Reasoning
lectures.description: How to read data, spot patterns, and not be fooled by statistics.

materials.title: Statistics Fundamentals (StatQuest)
materials.description: Mean, variance, distributions — explained with clarity.

materials.title: How to Lie with Statistics
materials.author: Darrell Huff, 1954
materials.description: A classic. Teaches critical thinking about data by showing how it's manipulated.
